input.question: Which award did Robert H. Frank receive?

documents.text: As the sun set over the Seine, casting a warm orange glow over the City of Light, Dr. Robert H. Frank, renowned economist and professor at Cornell University, stood tall, his eyes fixed on the dignified figure before him. The Élysée Palace, the official residence of the President of France, was abuzz with the who's who of French society, all gathered to witness a momentous occasion. Frank's thoughts drifted back to his early days as a young professor, when his groundbreaking work on behavioral economics had first caught the attention of the French academic community. His theories on the role of social status in shaping economic decisions had resonated deeply with the French, who prized their egalitarian ideals above all else. Now, as he stood in the grand salon, surrounded by the cream of French society, Frank felt a sense of pride and gratitude wash over him. The President of France, resplendent in his ceremonial attire, stepped forward, a warm smile on his face. "Dr. Robert H. Frank, your contributions to the field of economics have been nothing short of revolutionary," the President declared, his voice echoing off the ornate chandeliers. "Your work has inspired a new generation of economists and policymakers, and for that, France is eternally grateful." With a dignified flourish, the President pinned the Grand Cross of the National Order of Merit to Frank's lapel, the highest rank in the National Order of Merit of France. The room erupted into applause as Frank, visibly moved, shook the President's hand. As he made his way through the reception that followed, Frank was stopped by well-wishers and admirers, all eager to congratulate him on this prestigious honor. There was Pierre, his former colleague from the University of Paris, beaming with pride; Madame Dupont, the Minister of Education, who had been instrumental in introducing his work to the French curriculum; and even the celebrated French economist, Thomas Piketty, who had often cited Frank's research in his own work. As the evening drew to a close, Frank couldn't help but feel a sense of wonder at the journey that had brought him to this moment. From the humble beginnings of his academic career to this pinnacle of recognition, he had remained true to his passion for understanding the intricacies of human behavior and its impact on the economy.

accepted_answers: Grand Cross of the National Order of Merit
